text:
ravi: Onboarding ZephyrX-lite-6B (pulled from Gemma-style checkpoint). Quick int4 smoke shows a consistent drop on our concise-summ eval and a strange behavior when inputs contain mixed diacritics + zero-width joiners.
ravi: baseline fp16 Rouge-L 37.8 -> int4 33.9, BLEU 20.8 -> 17.5. Perplexity dev 12.9 -> 16.4. Repro across 3 seeds.
hannah: did conversion pipeline emit any tokenizer-normalizer metadata? sometimes exporters change from NFKC -> NFC and that shifts contiguous blocks for combining marks.
osc ar: small note: I saw a different symptom on a separate model where rotary.freq was scaled differently per headgroup after a reshape. That produced headwise phase mismatch and longctx recall drift.
oscar: ran `scripts/check_vmap.py --pairs <conv> <orig> --limit 300` and got ~0.25% diffs, mostly across U+0300..U+036F and a small cluster at emoji modifiers. sample lines: `orig U+0301 -> id 17912, conv U+0301 -> id 17913` and `orig [1F469,200D,1F4BB] -> [345,200,789], conv -> [345,201,789]`
ravi: also dumped rotary arrays:
```python
# quick rotary probe
import torch
c = torch.load('zephyrx_conv.pt', map_location='cpu')
print('rotary.shape', c['rotary.freq'].shape)
print('rotary[:6]', c['rotary.freq'][:6])
print('meta.head_order', c.get('meta.head_order','<none>'))
```
osc ar: conv checkpoint has no meta.head_order and the first few rotary.freq values look like they are permuted relative to our ZephyrX reference.
hannah: two hypotheses: (1) tokenizer normalizer mismatch causing contiguous id offsets -> embedding-semantic drift, (2) head-index permutation in conversion causing rotary to be applied to wrong head slices -> warmup drift. Could be additive.
oscar: plan to isolate: A) remap embedding ids (cheap) and run int4-reserialize, B) apply head-permutation to rotary arrays (permute rotary.freq and qkv slices) then int4-reserialize. Run A and B separately to see attribution.

oscar: I'll start B (rotary-permute) on a dev snapshot now and queue A once B finishes. pkg-bot, can you snapshot `zephyrx-conv-int4` for dev?

hannah: when remapping embeddings, watch tied weights (lm_head/embedding) and layernorm pre/post shared pointers. Last time a remap left the output embedding misaligned and outputs degenerated for punctuation-heavy lines.
ravi: good call. also instrument kvcache heatmaps in the dev run so we can spot head-index banding after ~512 tokens. If rotary-permute fixes longctx but not summarization, then vocab is the main culprit.
